rules: Reference fixture lead names, company values, rows, dates and counts are never copied into runtime state or submitted to the API.
Current lead, client, case and workspace IDs are read from existing runtime owners and preserved in task/event scope.
The prompt uses the existing task/event and activity sources; it does not create a parallel store or screenshot-only workflow.
A returned task/event ID is required before the lead next-action pointer is written.
Reference-image discrepancies never create per-window color exceptions. Semantic tones resolve through the canonical VST adapter.
The semantic delete base is --cf-vst-color-delete; strong, soft and border variants derive from it, and every trash/delete icon resolves to that family.
No fake success, no-op persistence model, automatic merge, silent fallback, unapproved browser mutation or production merge was introduced.

color_source_of_truth.policy: Each semantic concern has one VST token owner across every window and repeated component instance. Reference drift does not create local palette copies; all trash/delete icons share the same red delete family.

visible_controls_wired: Every prompt choice is controlled and rendered. The normal interactive Lead Detail entry validates choice/date/time, creates the supported task or event, requires the returned item ID, patches the lead pointer and records activity. Cancel, close and Escape close the prompt without persistence. The DEV preview disables Save and guards the handler as a no-op.
backend_boundary: Lead PATCH validates a supplied next_action_item_id in the current workspace and requires its lead relation to match. Task POST validates scoped lead/case/client relations and cross-entity consistency before insert. Task and event creation retain the current workspace/lead/client/case scope. Creation and subsequent lead/activity writes remain sequential existing API calls; a future server transaction could reduce orphan risk if a later write fails.
